title: Golgotha + Burial: Text and Candidate Traditions
subtitle: Textual constraints, Holy Sepulchre, and Garden Tomb kept separate
summary: Compare the unlocated Gospel Golgotha/tomb descriptions with the Holy Sepulchre tradition and the Garden Tomb alternative without assigning the textual locations their own coordinates.
disclaimer: The Gospels place crucifixion at Golgotha outside Jerusalem and burial in a nearby rock-cut tomb/garden context, but neither textual location receives a coordinate in the atlas. The Holy Sepulchre and Garden Tomb are displayed as separate traditions with different historical/archaeological considerations. No scene element proves a specific cross or tomb belonged to Jesus.

evidenceLegend.label: Physical geography
evidenceLegend.description: Established topography or measured terrain when a verified DEM is configured.

evidenceLegend.label: Known archaeology
evidenceLegend.description: Archaeological context represented only at the level supported by existing atlas records.

evidenceLegend.label: Historical inference
evidenceLegend.description: A historically reasoned reconstruction or orientation that is not an observed event location.

evidenceLegend.label: Tradition
evidenceLegend.description: A later Christian or local identification kept distinct from textual and archaeological certainty.

evidenceLegend.label: Unknown / disputed
evidenceLegend.description: An event point, route, building, or identification that cannot responsibly be fixed to one coordinate.

entryCamera.note: Frames the northwestern side of the Old City for comparison; it is not a Golgotha or tomb coordinate.

comparison.label: How should Golgotha and the burial place be mapped?
comparison.intro: Begin with the textual locations as unpinned, then inspect the two principal modern traditions as traditions rather than replacements for the textual records.

options.label: Textual Golgotha + tomb
options.summary: The Gospel execution and burial locations are geographically related in the narratives but not independently recoverable as exact modern points.
options.rationale: Keeping both records unpinned prevents a later tradition from becoming the hidden default.
options.objections: The map still needs a city-level display frame; that camera must not be treated as a candidate site.

camera.note: City-level orientation only; neither textual Golgotha nor the textual tomb is pinned here.

options.label: Holy Sepulchre tradition
options.summary: The Church of the Holy Sepulchre preserves the principal ancient Christian identification of both Golgotha and Jesus’ tomb.
options.rationale: Its long-standing tradition and quarry/tomb archaeological context make it historically serious and compatible with aspects of first-century topography.
options.objections: Compatibility and tradition do not prove that the exact venerated locations are the places of Jesus’ crucifixion and burial.

camera.note: Coordinates locate the modern/traditional Holy Sepulchre complex, not a proven crucifixion or tomb point.

options.label: Garden Tomb alternative
options.summary: The Garden Tomb is a modern Protestant alternative identification north of the Old City.
options.rationale: It is culturally and devotionally important and visually evokes a garden/tomb setting for many visitors.
options.objections: The tomb is commonly dated earlier than the first century CE, which weighs substantially against identifying it as the Gospel’s newly cut tomb.

camera.note: Coordinates locate the Garden Tomb tradition itself, not the textual tomb of Jesus.

hotspots.label: Golgotha — textual location, no pin
hotspots.summary: The crucifixion place is described in the Gospels but is not assigned a modern coordinate by the atlas.

whyShown.evidence: The execution place is textually named and associated with Jerusalem.
whyShown.inference: This is a display anchor inside the comparison frame, not a coordinate assigned to the Golgotha record.
whyShown.alternatives: Candidate/traditional sites are evaluated in separate comparison views.

hotspots.label: Tomb of Jesus — textual location, no pin
hotspots.summary: The burial narratives describe a rock-cut tomb near the crucifixion setting, but the atlas leaves the textual tomb unlocated.

whyShown.evidence: The Gospels place burial near the crucifixion setting and John mentions a garden.
whyShown.inference: The display anchor explains relational geography only; it is not stored as the tomb’s coordinate.

hotspots.label: Holy Sepulchre tradition
hotspots.summary: An ancient Christian site tradition whose physical context includes quarrying and rock-cut tombs predating the Constantinian complex.

whyShown.evidence: The site has a longstanding Christian identification and archaeologically relevant quarry/tomb context.
whyShown.inference: Those facts make the tradition historically serious but do not identify an individual tomb occupant or execution point.

hotspots.label: Quarry / tomb context
hotspots.summary: The area’s pre-Constantinian quarry and tomb context matters because it is compatible with a burial area outside the city in the relevant broad period reconstruction.

whyShown.evidence: Existing project research records quarry/tomb archaeology at the site.
whyShown.inference: Archaeological compatibility is not converted into proof of the Gospel identification.

hotspots.label: Garden Tomb alternative
hotspots.summary: A nineteenth-century alternative tradition displayed as its own site rather than as the textual tomb.

whyShown.evidence: The site is historically important as a modern devotional identification.
whyShown.inference: Its evocative landscape is not evidence that it is the Gospel tomb.
whyShown.alternatives: The commonly accepted earlier archaeological dating is a major objection.
